title: Capfolder 0.1.3: try it on a sample company

posts.label: Post
posts.text:
Would you type your cap table into an app you met today?

Most cap table tools ask exactly that on day one.
Share counts. Every founder. Every SAFE.
All before you've seen a single useful screen.

So Capfolder 0.1.3 lets you look first:

1. A sample company. Acme Inc. has 2 founders, 2 employees with options, an option pool and 3 SAFEs. Click anything. Nothing you do is saved.
2. Three yes/no questions. SAFEs? Option pool? Priced round? The steps that don't apply disappear.
3. A Get started list of 7 steps that ticks itself from what's in your cap table, so it never drifts out of date.
4. A 6-stop tour, and a "?" next to valuation cap, discount, cliff, par value and vesting start.

The sample even has 11 gaps in "What's missing" on purpose: the signed documents a lawyer would ask for. You see that list on fake data before it's about your company.

One honest limit: the sample is read-only, so you can't try e-signing in it.

Capfolder is free, open source, and keeps your cap table in a folder on your own computer.

Founders: when you first set up your cap table, what took the longest?

posts.label: Post
posts.text:
Let people try your app on fake data before they give you real data

I'm building Capfolder, an open-source cap table app. A cap table is about the most sensitive spreadsheet a startup has: who owns what, every investor, every SAFE amount.

The first versions started you on an empty cap table. To find out if you liked it, you had to type all of that in first. That's a big ask from an app you've known for five minutes, and it's a lot of work before you've seen anything useful.

What we did

Version 0.1.3 lets you look first:

  1. A sample company. One click opens a made-up company with 2 founders, 2 employees with options, an option pool and 3 SAFEs. Every screen works. Nothing you do is saved, and a banner on every screen says so.
  2. Three yes/no questions before setup (SAFEs? option pool? priced round?), so the steps that don't apply never show up.
  3. A Get started list of 7 steps that ticks itself from what's actually in your cap table.
  4. A 6-stop tour, and a "?" next to the jargon (valuation cap, discount, cliff, par value, vesting start).

The lesson: your test data is your demo

The sample company took far less work than I expected, because it already existed. It's the same made-up company our tests use to check the math, to the share. The app copies it into its own folder the first time you open it and refuses every save to it.

Two things I'd do again:

  • Make the demo show the problem, not just the product. The sample has 11 gaps in its "What's missing" list on purpose: the signed documents a lawyer would ask for. You see what the app catches before it's your company it's catching.
  • Never store checklist ticks. The Get started ticks are worked out from the cap table every time. A checklist you tick by hand goes out of date the day someone adds a SAFE somewhere else.

What I don't know yet

Whether it works. Your cap table never leaves your computer, so I can't watch people use it: I'll learn from people telling me. And the sample is read-only, so you can't try e-signing in it.

The full write-up, with screenshots: https://capfolder.com/blog/try-it-on-a-sample-company/

If your product handles sensitive data, how do you let people try it before they trust it?

posts.label: Article
posts.text:
Originally published on capfolder.com.

Capfolder is an open-source (AGPL) cap table app built with Tauri and React. Your cap table lives in a folder of plain files on your own computer: an append-only, hash-chained events.jsonl in the Open Cap Format, plus your signed PDFs.

That design made the first-run experience awkward. A new user opened an empty app and had to type in real share counts before seeing anything useful. In 0.1.3 we added a sample company, a self-ticking checklist and a tour. Here's how, in very little code.

1. The sample company is the test fixture

We already had a golden test company in fixtures/acme-vault/: the event log the engine must turn into an expected cap table CSV, to the share. The sample company is that same file. Vite's ?raw import bundles it as text, so no extra files ship:

import metaText from "../../../fixtures/acme-vault/capfolder.json?raw";
import eventsText from "../../../fixtures/acme-vault/events.jsonl?raw";

On first open it's copied into the app-data folder, with "sample": true added to capfolder.json. The event log is written last, so a half-made copy gets made again next time. Every document the events point to gets a one-page placeholder PDF from pdf-lib, so the Documents screen isn't full of "missing file" errors.

2. Read-only in one place

Every write in the app goes through the same append function, so read-only is one check there, not one per screen:

if (v.meta.sample) return [SAMPLE_BLOCKED];
// "This is the sample company, so nothing here is saved. Use Start my own to set up your company."

A banner on every screen says "Sample company · nothing here is real" with a Start my own button.

3. A checklist that never stores a tick

The Get started list has 7 steps. None of them is stored as done. Each one is worked out from the cap table state on every render:

{ label: "Founders and their shares", done: sec.some((x) => isFounder(s, x)) },
a.pool !== false && { label: "Option pool and grants", done: s.plans.size > 0 && sec.some((x) => x.kind === "equity") },
a.safes !== false && { label: "SAFEs", done: sec.some((x) => x.kind === "convertible") },

The a.pool and a.safes come from three yes/no questions asked before setup. Unanswered means "show the step", so skipping the questions never hides anything.

4. The tour

The tour is Driver.js (MIT) with six stops. skipMissingElement handles an empty company that has no holding row yet, and focus goes back to where it was when the tour closes.

What it doesn't do yet

The sample is read-only, so you can't try e-signing in it: signing goes through a relay, and we don't want fake envelopes there.

The code is on GitHub. If you've built a demo mode for a local-first app, how did you keep it from drifting away from the real thing?

A new cap table tool opens empty. To find out whether you trust it, you have to type in your real company first: share counts, founders, every SAFE. That's a lot of sensitive numbers for an app you met five minutes ago.

This week's release lets you look first.

A sample company. Pick "Try the sample company" and Capfolder opens Acme Inc.: 2 founders, 2 employees with options, an option pool and 3 SAFEs. Click any row to see how its vesting is worked out. Nothing you do is saved.

It even has 11 gaps in "What's missing" on purpose: the signed documents a lawyer would ask for in due diligence. Better to see that list on fake data first.

Three quick questions. SAFEs? Option pool? Priced round? The setup steps that don't apply disappear.

A Get started list. Seven steps that tick themselves from what's in your cap table, each with the button that does it.

A one-minute tour with six stops, and a "?" next to valuation cap, discount, cliff, par value and vesting start.
